newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: ALYTAUS TEXTILE JAN-APRIL SALES UP.
newsitem.headline: ALYTAUS TEXTILE JAN-APRIL SALES UP.

text.p: Lithuania's cotton material producer Alytaus Textile said on Wednesday that its sales advanced to 61.1 million litas during the first four months of the year compared to 34.9 million litas in the same period in 1996.
The company's director of finances Grazhina Ludavichiene also said that the company's sales in the first quarter of 1997 were 42.4 million litas.
"The company could increase its turnover even more but has a lack of working capital," Ludavichiene said.
Ludavichiene declined to mention any profit figures.
The Lithuanian stock exchange told Reuters that the company posted 23.02 million litas in losses in 1996 on turnover of 124.4 million litas.

The company exports 80 percent of its products to Western Europe and Scandinavia, five percent to CIS countries, Latvia and Estonia and the remaining 15 percent are sold on the local market, Ludavichiene said.
The company is listed on the A group of the Vilnius bourse, where 212,000 litas worth of its shares changed hands Tuesday. Dealers said that Hansa Investment was behind the purchase.
Around 63 percent percent of the company is state-owned and Lithuanian government has slated it for privatisation.
